Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:

- Policy stance and macro tone: The Committee’s hold at 5.25–5.50% with “some further progress” toward 2% and ongoing QT (IOER 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, caps $25B Treasuries/$35B MBS) keeps financial conditions restrictive.

- SLOOS overlay (July 2024):
  - C&I loans: Banks on net reported tighter standards/terms (including wider loan-rate spreads) and weaker demand from firms of all sizes, citing a less certain economic outlook and reduced risk tolerance.
  - CRE loans: Further tightening across CRE categories, with particularly weak demand for office-related lending; ongoing credit discipline remains a notable headwind.
  - RRE/HELOCs: Standards remained tight for most residential mortgage categories (including government mortgages) and HELOCs; spreads elevated; underwriting remains conservative.
  - Consumer credit: Banks reported tighter standards for credit card, auto, and other consumer loans. Many raised minimum required credit scores and minimum payment requirements and noted rising delinquencies/charge-offs from low levels, alongside weaker loan demand.

- Implications for tone: SLOOS points to persistent credit supply headwinds that complement the Fed’s restrictive stance and QT, tempering the otherwise cautiously positive macro message. This supports the Committee’s “better balance of risks” language but argues for a more guarded interpretation of growth momentum and household credit health.

Net effect: Slightly positive on disinflation and growth, but more cautious due to tighter bank lending and softer loan demand across categories.
